findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC was unable to provide information verifying that the food handler at the time of food preparation what completed the Certified Food Protection Manager course and passed the test. The situation was discussed and they were instructed to have sufficient CFPMs available to cover all food preparation shifts in the facility and to maintain copies of these certification at the facility for verification.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide proof that employee were notified in a verifiable manner their need to provide information related to foodborne illnesses related to themselves. The PIC was instructed to provide this information prior to the scheduled follow up.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code. 

Containers of frozen foods in the walk in freezer were observed open and with ice condensate from the condenser unit inside of the packaging and in contact with the foods. The PIC was shown and discarded the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. The PIC was instructed to ensure that all foods are protected from contamination at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) (REPEAT) Multiple nozzles of the fountain drink machines were observed heavily soiled during this inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned all nozzles during this inspection to correct. These items should be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitized) daily or every other day moving forward. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch at all times in the facility. 2) The blade of the can opener in the kitchen was observed with food debris stuck to it. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean at all times in the facility. The blade was cleaned during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

Single service boats were observed in front of the fryers. They had the food contact surfaces up/exposed. These items need to be stored face down at least so that drips, splash or other contaminates are not a concern for contaminating the food contact surface. The PIC was shown and instructed to store the single service items in such a way as to protect them from contamination moving froward.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide test strips for the sanitizer used in the facility. Education was conducted and they were instructed to acquire the test strips prior to the scheduled follow up.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

1) (REPEAT) Major ice and frost accumulation was observed in the walk in freezer. 2) The shelving where the trash cans were stored in the customer areas was observed heavily soiled on the bottoms as well as on the walls and doors. 3) Dust was observed on the fan covers in the walk in cooler sufficient that sections appeared ready to fly off and potentially contaminate foods. The PIC was shown all noted locations and instructed to review cleaning procedures and ensure that cleaning is taking place thoroughly and regularly moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). 

The coving at the floor/wall junction below the fountain drink machines was observed pulling away from the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair/replace the coving prior to the next routine inspection and maintain the physical facility in a state of good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Nozzles of the fountain drink machine are observed soiled during this inspection. The PIC was shown and replaced all nozzles during this inspection with the back ups to correct. Per the PIC the nozzles are cleaned weekly. This should be more often as the needs of the facility require. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

The ambient air thermometer in the prep cooler is observed broken and non-functioning at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and placed another thermometer in the cooler to correct the violation. Ensure that all coolers have a correctly functioning thermometer available in them at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

1) Major ice and frost accumulation is observed in the walk in freezer. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and to clean often enough to maintain the area free of frost and ice. 2) The floor in the walk in cooler has filth accumulation in corners that needs to be clean more thoroughly. The PIC was shown and instructed review cleaning procedures and ensure that cleaning is taking place thoroughly and regularly moving forward.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of this inspection there is not a CFPM on site. Pizzas were observed coming out of the oven and being sliced then displayed. Food handling activities are taking place. Ensure that there is a CFPM available at all times that foods are being handled/prepared. Acquire enough CFPMs prior to the next routine inspection in order to cover all times of food handling/preparation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival there were not any paper towels available for hand washing in the kitchen. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the available dispenser was refilled to correct.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

During this inspection the PIC could not show food handler cards for employees at the facility. One employee is still in their training period and is not being considered at this time but the other two could not show completed food handler training. Food handler certificates are on the networked system for Road Ranger. Ensure that all employees that handle RTE or TCS foods have completed food handler training and that the certificates are available prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cheeses and meats in the open faced end cap cooler are observed with temperatures ranging in the 50s-60s. The PIC removed all of the items from this cooler and is in the process of wasting them. A work order has been placed for repairs on this cooler.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The cooler noted on line item #22 needs repaired so that it can maintain effective cold holding temperatures. Follow up is being set for two weeks for compliance.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed soiled. PIC indicated that weekly cleaning takes place for these items and that it will be changed to bi-weekly after this. The items were replaced with clean ones and the soiled ones moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

A spray bottle behind the service counter is without a label indicating the chemical stored within. PIC indicated that it was window cleaner and a label was added to the bottle to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival the bottle of sanitizer hooked up to the dispenser in the kitchen was empty. A new bottle was added to the dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use at all times that foods (and food contact) are being handled and prepared.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Two unlabeled spray bottles observed (one in the kitchen, one behind the service counter). CORRECTED- According to PIC, spray bottle in the kitchen contains oven cleaner and was labeled as such. Counter spray bottle contained water and was emptied.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]
